title: 25.5 A 99.5mW/Port DC-to-40GHz Integrated Channel Analyzer for High-Density Signal Integrity Measurement in 28nm CMOS
problem: High-speed electrical links (PCB traces, coaxial cables) in dense Ethernet switches and high-performance computers suffer from reflection, crosstalk, and insertion loss; traditional VNAs and sampling oscilloscopes are power-hungry, expensive, and inefficient.
motivation: Dense channel environments in modern data-center networks require low-power, integrated signal-integrity (SI) measurement to detect link defects without expensive external test equipment.
method: The analyzer uses two pulse-based measurement techniques: time-domain reflectometry (sending a pulse down a wire and measuring echoes to detect impedance mismatches) and time-domain transmission (measuring the signal that reaches the far end) to measure signal degradation on high-speed electrical connections. Both techniques are integrated into a single application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) using 28-nanometer CMOS process technology, allowing four measurement ports to fit on one device. The system covers frequencies from DC (direct current) to 40GHz with a 9.1 picosecond response time, consuming only 99.5 milliwatts per port.
key_novelty: A single application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) with four measurement ports characterizes signal degradation on high-speed data links from DC to 40GHz while consuming only 99.5 milliwatts per port.
contributions: 9.1ps rise time for fine temporal resolution
primary_theme: On-chip signal-integrity measurement for high-speed links
